work: Enarratio in Epistolam II B. Pauli ad Timotheum
source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. XIII (Montreuil)

1.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI PRIMI : PAULUS APOSTOLUS JESU CHRISTI PER VOLUNTATEM DEI.
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God.

paras.t: PAULUS apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei, id est Deo agente, secundum promissionem vitæ, id est propter præmium, vel ad obtinendam remunerationem vitæ quæ est in Christo Jesu, id est vitæ æternæ, quæ a Christo confertur, et in Christo consistit sicut in objecto: quæ vita est præmium, propter quod factus sum apostolus, non ab homine, sed a Deo: mandat et scribit Timotheo carissimo filio suo spirituali. Gratia gratum faciens, misericordia, id est peccatorum remissio, et pax, id est tranquillitas mentis, sit tibi a Deo Patre et Christo Jesu filio ejus Domino nostro.
paras.en: [[1:1|Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God|PAULUS apostolus Jesu Christi per voluntatem Dei]], that is, by God's doing, [[1:1|according to the promise of life|secundum promissionem vitæ]], that is, for the sake of the reward, or to obtain the recompense of the life [[1:1|which is in Christ Jesus|quæ est in Christo Jesu]], that is, of life everlasting, which is bestowed by Christ and consists in Christ as in its object: which life is the reward for whose sake I was made an apostle, not by man but by God: commands and writes [[1:2|To Timothy, my dearly beloved son|Timotheo carissimo filio]], his spiritual son. [[1:2|Grace|Gratia]] that makes pleasing [*gratia gratum faciens*, sanctifying grace, which makes the soul pleasing to God], [[1:2|mercy|misericordia]], that is, the remission of sins, [[1:2|and peace|et pax]], that is, tranquillity of mind, be to thee [[1:2|from God the Father and from Christ Jesus|a Deo Patre et Christo Jesu]] his Son, [[1:2|our Lord|Domino nostro]].

paras.t: Gratias ago Deo meo, cui servio a progenitoribus meis, id est exemplo antiquorum patrum meorum, videlicet Abrahæ, Isaac et Jacob, quorum vestigia imitor unum verum Deum colendo, in conscientia pura, id est sine remorsu alicujus peccati. Inde autem gratias ago, quod sine intermissione, id est omni congruo tempore, habeam tui memoriam in orationibus meis fusis pro te et aliis, nocte ac die;
paras.en: [[1:3|I give thanks to God|Gratias ago Deo meo]] [Denis reads *Deo meo*, "to my God"], [[1:3|whom I serve from my forefathers|cui servio a progenitoribus meis]], that is, after the example of my fathers of old, namely Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, in whose footsteps I follow by worshipping the one true God, [[1:3|with a pure conscience|in conscientia pura]], that is, without remorse for any sin. And I give thanks for this, [[1:3|that without ceasing|quod sine intermissione]], that is, at every fitting time, [[1:3|I have a remembrance of thee in my prayers|habeam tui memoriam in orationibus meis]] poured out for thee and for others, [[1:3|night and day|nocte ac die]];

paras.t: desiderans te videre, memor lacrymarum, quas deduxerunt oculi tui quando recessi a te, qui libentissime mecum transisses ac permansisses, ut gaudio implear, id est, ut te in bonis confirmem, et accendam ad martyrii palmam, quo facto, de tuo profectu plene exsultem; recordationem accipiens ejus fidei quæ est in te non ficta, id est tuæ veræ fidei reminiscens, quæ non est simulata, sed pura et efficax; quæ fides et habitavit, id est, firmiter fuit, primum in avia tua Loide, id est matre matris tuæ sic dicta; habitavit quoque et in matre tua Eunice. Parentum fidem commemorat, ut fidem filii roboret. Tacet vero de patre Timothei, quoniam gentilis erat et infidelis, ut dicitur. Certus sum autem quod et in te habitet fides ista.
paras.en: [[1:4|Desiring to see thee|desiderans te videre]], [[1:4|being mindful of thy tears|memor lacrymarum]], which thine eyes shed[[Jer 9:18||]] [the margin gives Jer. xx, 12, which does not fit; the phrase recalls Jer 9:18, "let our eyes shed tears"] when I went away from thee, thou who wouldst most gladly have gone along with me and stayed with me; [[1:4|that I may be filled with joy|ut gaudio implear]], that is, that I may confirm thee in good things and kindle thee toward the palm of martyrdom, and, that done, may rejoice fully in thy progress; [[1:5|Calling to mind that faith which is in thee unfeigned|recordationem accipiens ejus fidei quæ est in te non ficta]], that is, remembering thy true faith, which is not feigned but pure and effective; [[1:5|which also dwelt|quæ fides et habitavit]], that is, was firmly, [[1:5|first in thy grandmother Lois|primum in avia tua Loide]], that is, thy mother's mother, so called; it dwelt also [[1:5|and in thy mother Eunice|et in matre tua Eunice]]. He recalls the faith of the parents to strengthen the faith of the son. But he is silent about Timothy's father, because he was a Gentile and an unbeliever, as is said[[Acts 16:1||]]. And [[1:5|I am certain that in thee also|Certus sum autem quod et in te habitet fides ista]] this faith dwells.

paras.t: Propter quam causam, videlicet, quia tam bonas genitrices habuisti, et fidelis diu fuisti, admoneo te paterne, ut resuscites, id est, reformes, perficere studeas, et ad pristinos actus extendas, gratiam Dei quæ est in te, id est gratiam episcopalem et sacramentalem tibi divinitus datam in tui ordinatione vel confirmatione, per impositionem manuum […] quæ tibi positio fuit causa gratiæ dispositiva et instrumentalis. Vel potest intelligi absolute de gratia gratificante, quia per impositionem manuum Apostolorum dabatur Spiritus Sanctus. Ex his patet, quod gratia in corde Timothei erat quasi sopita et debilitata: ideo admonet eum ut reparet gratiam pristinam, proficiendo in ea. Unde etiam quod in Apocalypsi angelo Ecclesiæ Ephesi dicitur, Scio opera tua et laborem et patientiam; et post pauca, Sed habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti; memor esto itaque unde exciderit, et age pœnitentiam, et prima opera fac: quidam exponunt de Timotheo, quem constat fuisse Ephesiorum angelum, id est episcopum.
paras.en: [[1:6|For which cause|Propter quam causam]], namely, because thou hadst such good mothers [*genitrices*: his mother and grandmother] and hast long been faithful, [[1:6|I admonish thee|admoneo te]] as a father, [[1:6|that thou stir up|ut resuscites]], that is, renew, strive to perfect, and stretch out to its former acts, [[1:6|the grace of God which is in thee|gratiam Dei quæ est in te]], that is, the episcopal and sacramental grace given thee by God in thy ordination or confirmation, [[1:6|by the imposition of my hands|per impositionem manuum]] […]; which imposition was for thee a disposing and instrumental cause of grace. Or it may be understood simply of sanctifying grace [*gratia gratificans*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God], because by the imposition of the hands of the Apostles the Holy Ghost was given[[Acts 8:17||]]. From this it is plain that grace in Timothy's heart was as it were asleep and weakened: therefore he admonishes him to repair his former grace by making progress in it. Hence also what is said in the Apocalypse to the angel of the Church of Ephesus, [[Apoc 2:2|I know thy works and thy labour and thy patience|Scio opera tua et laborem et patientiam]]; and a little after, [[Apoc 2:4|But I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first charity|Sed habeo adversum te, quod caritatem tuam primam reliquisti]]; [[Apoc 2:5|Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen: and do penance and do the first works|memor esto itaque unde exciderit, et age pœnitentiam, et prima opera fac]]: some expound of Timothy, who is known to have been the angel, that is, the bishop, of the Ephesians.

paras.t: Non enim dedit nobis Deus spiritum, id est donum, timoris pure servilis; vel, Spiritum timoris, id est animam inordinate timentem temporalia mala, videlicet eos qui corpus occidunt; sed dedit nobis spiritum, id est donum et gratiam, virtutis, id est fortitudinis contra adversa, quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, et dilectionis Dei ac proximi, et sobrietatis, id est temperantiæ vel discretionis. Verba hæc plenius exposita sunt ad Romanos, ubi legitur, Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore.
paras.en: [[1:7|For God hath not given us the spirit|Non enim dedit nobis Deus spiritum]], that is, the gift, [[1:7|of fear|timoris]] that is purely servile [servile fear: fear of punishment alone, as against the filial fear of offending God]; or, *the spirit of fear*, that is, a soul that inordinately fears temporal evils, namely [[Matt 10:28|them that kill the body|eos qui corpus occidunt]]; [[1:7|but|sed]] he hath given us the spirit, that is, the gift and grace, [[1:7|of power|virtutis]], that is, of fortitude against adversities, which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[1:7|and of love|et dilectionis]] of God and of neighbour, [[1:7|and of sobriety|et sobrietatis]], that is, of temperance or discretion. These words are more fully expounded on the Epistle to the Romans, where we read, [[Rom 8:15|you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear|Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore]].

paras.t: Noli itaque erubescere, id est, quoniam dedit nobis Deus spiritum dilectionis, non erubescas testimonium Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est protestationem, prædicationem seu confessionem Christi; sed sine rubore et confusione testare coram hominibus, quod Christus sit Deus et homo, qui sua passione universum mundum redemit, resurrexit, cœlos ascendit. Unde ait Salvator in Evangelio: Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo; et rursus, Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet. Neque erubescas me vinctum ejus, id est me Paulum pro fide nunc captum atque ligatum.
paras.en: [[1:8|Be not thou therefore ashamed|Noli itaque erubescere]]: that is, since God hath given us the spirit of love, be not ashamed [[1:8|of the testimony of our Lord|testimonium Domini nostri]] Jesus Christ, that is, of the witness, preaching or confession of Christ; but without blushing or confusion bear witness before men that Christ is God and man, who by his passion redeemed the whole world, rose again, and ascended into heaven. Hence the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:32|that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father|Qui me confessus fuerit coram hominibus, confitebor et ego eum coram Patre meo]]; and again, [[Luke 9:26|he that shall be ashamed of me and of my words, of him the Son of man shall be ashamed|Qui me erubuerit et meos sermones, hunc Filius hominis erubescet]]. Nor be ashamed [[1:8|of me his prisoner|me vinctum ejus]], that is, of me, Paul, now taken and bound for the faith.

paras.t: Sed collabora Evangelio, id est, cum me et ceteris evangelizantibus, labora ad promulgationem ac venerationem evangelicæ legis, fortiter prædicando, juste vivendo, et pro fidei veritate mortem sustinendo, secundum virtutem Dei, id est secundum virtutem et gratiam tibi divinitus datam; qui nos liberavit per propriam passionem a jugo diaboli et pœna inferni, et vocavit ad fidem ac vitam æternam, vocatione sua sancta, id est inspiratione interna (de qua in Apocalypsi: Ego sto ad ostium et pulso), vel prædicatione evangelica quam fecit per nos: non enim nos sumus qui loquimur, sed Spiritus Patris nostri qui loquitur in nobis. Vocavit, inquam, nos, non secundum opera nostra, id est propria merita, quæ vocationem hanc nequaquam præcesserunt, sed secundum propositum suum, id est voluntatis suæ decretum seu voluntariam præordinationem, et gratiam nobis clementer infusam: quæ est effectus hujus propositi, per quem ad omnia opera meritoria promovemur atque perducimur; quæ data, id est dari præordinata, est nobis in Christo Jesu, id est per Christum, utputa per ejus incarnationem, virtutem et meritum, ante tempora sæcularia, id est ab æterno.
paras.en: But [[1:8|labour with the gospel|collabora Evangelio]], that is, labour with me and the other preachers of the gospel for the spreading and honouring of the gospel law, by preaching boldly, living justly, and suffering death for the truth of the faith, [[1:8|according to the power of God|secundum virtutem Dei]], that is, according to the power and grace given thee by God; [[1:9|Who hath delivered us|qui nos liberavit]] by his own passion from the yoke of the devil and the punishment of hell, [[1:9|and called us|et vocavit]] to faith and life everlasting, [[1:9|by his holy calling|vocatione sua sancta]], that is, by inward inspiration (of which it is said in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 3:20|I stand at the gate and knock|Ego sto ad ostium et pulso]]), or by the preaching of the gospel which he did through us: for it is not we that speak, but the Spirit of our Father that speaketh in us[[Matt 10:20||]] [Christ's words in Matt 10:20, which Denis puts in the first person]. He called us, I say, [[1:9|not according to our own works|non secundum opera nostra]], that is, our own merits, which in no way went before this calling, [[1:9|but according to his own purpose|sed secundum propositum suum]], that is, the decree of his will or his free foreordaining, [[1:9|and grace|et gratiam nobis]] mercifully poured into us: which is the effect of this purpose, by which we are moved and brought on to all meritorious works; [[1:9|which was given|quæ data]], that is, foreordained to be given, [[1:9|us in Christ Jesus|est nobis in Christo Jesu]], that is, through Christ, namely through his incarnation, power and merit, [[1:9|before the times of the world|ante tempora sæcularia]], that is, from eternity.

paras.t: Manifestata est autem, id est, publice prædicata et nota, vel evidenter impleta est, nunc tempore gratiæ, per illuminationem, id est prædicationem et doctrinam, Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi: quam proprio ore vel per Apostolos mundo proposuit, aut certe per illuminationem factam in die Pentecostes, quando in igneis linguis Spiritus Sanctus apparens, illuminavit Apostolos ad cognoscendum et prædicandum hanc gratiam: quæ illuminatio dicitur Christi, quoniam ipse misit Spiritum Sanctum. Qui Christus sua passione destruxit, id est hominibus abstulit, mortem culpæ atque gehennæ, et corporis immortalitatem promeruit eis: quam et nunc præstat in spe, daturus eam in re quando corruptibile hoc induet incorruptionem. Hoc est quod apud Osee loquitur: De morte redimam eos; ero mors tua, o mors. Illuminavit autem, id est, notam fecit, vitam æternam, quæ est merces nostri laboris, et finis hujus peregrinationis, et incorruptionem, id est perpetuam immortalitatem, quam habebunt electi in anima et corpore post diem judicii, per Evangelium, id est Evangelii prædicationem, videlicet per se ipsum et discipulos suos, dicendo: Cognosco oves meas, et vitam æternam do eis; et alibi, Qui credit in me, non morietur in æternum. In quo Evangelio prædicando, videlicet ut id annuntiem omnibus, positus sum ego, id est a Deo ordinatus et constitutus, prædicator et apostolus et magister gentium.
paras.en: [[1:10|But is now made manifest|Manifestata est autem]], that is, publicly preached and known, or plainly fulfilled, [[1:10|now|nunc]] in the time of grace, [[1:10|by the illumination|per illuminationem]], that is, the preaching and teaching, [[1:10|of our Saviour Jesus Christ|Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi]], which he set before the world with his own mouth or through the Apostles; or else by the illumination made on the day of Pentecost, when the Holy Ghost, appearing in tongues of fire, enlightened the Apostles to know and to preach this grace[[Acts 2:3||]] [the margin gives Acts ii, 1–4]: which illumination is called Christ's, since he himself sent the Holy Ghost[[John 16:7||]]. Christ by his passion [[1:10|hath destroyed|destruxit]], that is, took away from men, [[1:10|death|mortem]] of guilt and of hell, and merited for them the immortality of the body: which he gives even now in hope, and will give in reality when this corruptible shall put on incorruption. This is what is said in Osee: [[Osee 13:14|I will redeem them from death|De morte redimam eos]]; [[Osee 13:14|O death, I will be thy death|ero mors tua, o mors]]. [[1:10|and hath brought to light|Illuminavit autem]], that is, made known, [[1:10|life|vitam æternam]] everlasting, which is the reward of our labour and the end of this pilgrimage, [[1:10|and incorruption|et incorruptionem]], that is, everlasting immortality, which the elect will have in soul and body after the day of judgement, [[1:10|by the gospel|per Evangelium]], that is, by the preaching of the gospel, namely through himself and his disciples, saying: I know my sheep[[John 10:27||]], and [[John 10:28|I give them life everlasting|vitam æternam do eis]]; and elsewhere, He that [[John 11:26|believeth in me shall not die for ever|credit in me, non morietur in æternum]] [the margin reads Ibid. v, 26; the words are John 11:26]. [[1:11|Wherein|In quo]] gospel, that is, in preaching it, namely that I may announce it to all, [[1:11|I am appointed|positus sum ego]], that is, ordained and established by God, [[1:11|a preacher and an apostle and teacher of the Gentiles|prædicator et apostolus et magister gentium]].

paras.t: Ob quam causam etiam, videlicet propter Evangelii prædicationem, hæc, id est incarcerationem, ligationem et alia plurima, patior; sed non confundor in me ipso, quasi turpe aliquid operans: imo glorior in adversis. Verbum equidem crucis pereuntibus stultitia est; his vero qui salvi fiunt, id est nobis, virtus Dei est. Scio enim cui credidi, scilicet Deo omnipotenti, qui est via, veritas et vita, et certus sum quia potens est depositum meum, id est beatitudinem mihi paratam, quam merui et apud ipsum reposui, servare in illum diem, id est usque ad diem remunerationis meæ, hoc est usque ad diem mortis, quantum ad glorificationem animæ, et usque in diem extremi judicii, quantum ad glorificationem corporis mei.
paras.en: [[1:12|For which cause, I also|Ob quam causam etiam]], namely on account of the preaching of the gospel, [[1:12|suffer|patior]] [[1:12|these things|hæc]], that is, imprisonment, binding and very many other things; [[1:12|but I am not ashamed|sed non confundor]] in myself, as though doing something shameful: nay, I glory in adversities. For indeed [[1 Cor 1:18|the word of the cross, to them indeed that perish, is foolishness|Verbum equidem crucis pereuntibus stultitia est]]: [[1 Cor 1:18|but to them that are saved, that is, to us, it is the power of God|his vero qui salvi fiunt, id est nobis, virtus Dei est]]. [[1:12|For I know whom I have believed|Scio enim cui credidi]], namely almighty God, who is [[John 14:6|the way, and the truth, and the life|via, veritas et vita]], [[1:12|and I am certain that he is able|et certus sum quia potens est]] [[1:12|to keep|servare]] [[1:12|that which I have committed unto him|depositum meum]], that is, the beatitude prepared for me, which I have merited and laid up with him, [[1:12|against that day|in illum diem]], that is, until the day of my reward: that is, until the day of death as regards the glorification of the soul, and until the day of the last judgement as regards the glorification of my body.

paras.t: Insuper admonet Timotheum. Formam habens sanorum verborum, id est tu, Timothee, habens seriem sanctarum prædicationum, seu formam evangelicorum verborum, quæ verba a me prædicante audisti: habens, inquam, hæc verba in fide, id est cum fidei observatione, et dilectione in Christo Jesu, id est per gratiam Christi ad gloriam ejus, vel secundum voluntatem ipsius, bonum depositum custodi, id est, gratiam tibi concessam conserva, et officium tibi commissum digne prosequere. Vel sic: Bonum depositum de quo nunc dixi, id est præmium tibi apud Deum repositum pro tuo labore, custodi, ne illud per negligentiam perdas. Per Spiritum Sanctum, id est, non tuis viribus, sed adjutorio Spiritus Sancti hoc age, qui habitat in nobis per caritatem et gratiam, quoniam sumus templum Dei. Dominus enim in templo sancto suo.
paras.en: He further admonishes Timothy. [[1:13|Hold the form of sound words|Formam habens sanorum verborum]] [Denis reads *habens*, "having", for the Vulgate's *habe*, "hold"], that is, thou, Timothy, having the course of holy preachings, or the form of the gospel words, [[1:13|which thou hast heard of me|quæ verba a me prædicante audisti]] as I preached: having, I say, these words [[1:13|in faith|in fide]], that is, with the keeping of the faith, [[1:13|and in the love which is in Christ Jesus|et dilectione in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the grace of Christ unto his glory, or according to his will, [[1:14|Keep the good thing committed to thy trust|bonum depositum custodi]], that is, preserve the grace granted to thee, and carry out worthily the office entrusted to thee. Or thus: the good deposit of which I have just spoken, that is, the reward laid up for thee with God for thy labour, keep, lest thou lose it through negligence. [[1:14|by the Holy Ghost|Per Spiritum Sanctum]], that is, not by thy own strength, but do this by the help of the Holy Ghost, [[1:14|who dwelleth in us|qui habitat in nobis]] by charity and grace, since we are the temple of God[[1 Cor 3:16||]][[1 Cor 3:17||]]. For [[Ps 10:5|The Lord is in his holy temple|Dominus enim in templo sancto suo]].

paras.t: Scis hoc, id est, jam plane agnoscis, vel scire debes, quod aversi sunt a me omnes qui in Asia sunt, id est, quod universi qui nunc recesserunt a me cum perfido corde, sunt in Asia minori; ex quibus, id est de quorum numero, sunt Phigelus et Hermogenes. Hi, ut legitur, fraudulenter accesserunt Apostolum ut discerent ejus mysteria, quatenus materiam calumniandi haberent: qui quum se manifestatos conspicerent, abierunt.
paras.en: [[1:15|Thou knowest this|Scis hoc]], that is, thou now plainly recognisest it, or oughtest to know it, [[1:15|that all they who are in Asia are turned away from me|quod aversi sunt a me omnes qui in Asia sunt]], that is, that all who have now gone away from me with faithless heart are in Asia Minor; [[1:15|of whom|ex quibus]], that is, of whose number, [[1:15|are Phigellus|sunt Phigelus]] and [[1:15|Hermogenes|Hermogenes]]. These, as we read, came to the Apostle deceitfully to learn his mysteries, so that they might have matter for calumny; and when they saw themselves found out, they went away.

paras.t: Det misericordiam Dominus Onesiphori domui, id est fideli familiæ Onesiphori Asiani, quia sæpe me refrigeravit, id est, consolatus est et refocillavit, necessaria ministrando, et catenam meam, id est me catenis vinctum, non erubuit verecundando de tali magistro; sed quum Romam venisset, sollicite me quæsivit et invenit.
paras.en: [[1:16|The Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus|Det misericordiam Dominus Onesiphori domui]], that is, to the faithful household of Onesiphorus of Asia, [[1:16|because he hath often refreshed me|quia sæpe me refrigeravit]], that is, comforted and revived me by supplying my needs; and [[1:16|of my chain|catenam meam]], that is, of me bound with chains, he [[1:16|hath not been ashamed|non erubuit]], blushing for such a master; [[1:17|But when he was come to Rome, he carefully sought me and found me|sed quum Romam venisset, sollicite me quæsivit et invenit]].

paras.t: Det illi Dominus Pater invenire misericordiam, id est gratiam adipisci et vitam æternam a Domino Filio: cui Pater dedit omne judicium, juxta illud: Deus, judicium tuum regi da; in illa die, id est in die mortis atque judicii. Talis modus loquendi in veteri Testamento usitatior est, ut ibi: Pluit Dominus super Sodomam ignem et sulphur a Domino. Et quanta beneficia Ephesi, id est in Epheso, ministraverit mihi Onesiphorus iste, tu melius nosti qui præsens fuisti, quam ea quæ Romæ mihi ministraverit.
paras.en: [[1:18|The Lord grant unto him|Det illi Dominus]] the Father [[1:18|to find mercy|invenire misericordiam]], that is, to obtain grace and life everlasting, [[1:18|of the Lord|a Domino Filio]] the Son, to whom the Father [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment|dedit omne judicium]], according to that saying: [[Ps 71:2|Give to the king thy judgment, O God|Deus, judicium tuum regi da]]; [[1:18|in that day|in illa die]], that is, in the day of death and of judgement. This manner of speaking [the Lord giving from the Lord] is more usual in the Old Testament, as there: [[Gen 19:24|the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord|Pluit Dominus super Sodomam ignem et sulphur a Domino]]. [[1:18|And in how many things|Et quanta beneficia]] [[1:18|at Ephesus|Ephesi]], that is, in Ephesus, [[1:18|he ministered unto me|ministraverit mihi]], this Onesiphorus, [[1:18|thou very well knowest|tu melius nosti]], who wast there, better than those which he ministered to me at Rome [Denis takes *melius*, "better", as a comparative: thou knowest his services at Ephesus better than those at Rome].

2.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : TU ERGO, FILI MI, CONFORTARE IN GRATIA.
2.title_en: Elucidation of the second chapter: Thou therefore, my son, be strong in grace.

paras.t: Tu ergo, fili mi, confortare in gratia gratum faciente: quæ est omnium operum meritoriorum principium, sicut natura est principium operationum naturalium; quæ gratia est in Christo Jesu sicut in fonte et capite, quia ab ipso derivatur in nos. De plenitudine quippe ejus omnes accepimus.
paras.en: [[2:1|Thou therefore, my son, be strong|Tu ergo, fili mi, confortare]] in grace, sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God], which is the principle of all meritorious works, as nature is the principle of natural operations; which grace is [[2:1|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]] as in its fountain and head, because from Him it flows down into us. For [[John 1:16|of his fulness we all have received|De plenitudine quippe ejus omnes accepimus]].

paras.t: Et quæ audisti a me, id est evangelica documenta quæ tibi proposui, per multos testes, id est per allegationes Prophetarum, quorum testimonio confirmavi quæ docui; vel, Per multos testes, id est multis præsentibus qui testimonium ferre possent; hæc commenda fidelibus hominibus ut prædicent aliis, non quibuscumque fidelibus, sed qui idonei erunt et alios docere, id est, qui morum probitate, scientia atque facundia pollent.
paras.en: [[2:2|And the things which thou hast heard of me|Et quæ audisti a me]], that is, the gospel teachings which I set before thee, [[2:2|by many witnesses|per multos testes]], that is, by citing the Prophets, by whose testimony I confirmed what I taught; or, *By many witnesses*, that is, with many present who could bear witness; [[2:2|the same commend to faithful men|hæc commenda fidelibus hominibus]], that they may preach to others: not to any faithful at all, but to those [[2:2|who shall be fit to teach others also|qui idonei erunt et alios docere]], that is, who excel in uprightness of life, in knowledge and in eloquence.

paras.t: Labora in agro dominico et vinea Domini Sabaoth, sicut bonus miles Christi Jesu, spinas vitiorum et tribulos passionum de cordibus subditorum evellendo, vita et labiis prædicando, et tuum officium digne continuando.
paras.en: [[2:3|Labour|Labora]] in the Lord's field and in the vineyard of the Lord of Sabaoth, [[2:3|as a good soldier of Christ Jesus|sicut bonus miles Christi Jesu]], plucking out the thorns of vices and the thistles of the passions from the hearts of those in thy charge, preaching by life and by lips, and worthily carrying on thy office.

paras.t: Nemo militans Deo, id est ad Dei honorem et gloriam, adversariis veritatis repugnans, contra propria vitia luctans, et divinis exercitiis se immergens, implicat, id est involvit, se negotiis sæcularibus, id est causis et rebus divitiisque mundanis. Per hoc enim distraheretur mens ejus ab illo uno quod solum necessarium est. Ideo sollicitudo de crastino prohibetur a Christo. Nam etsi interim oporteat servum et militem Christi sæcularia tractare negotia, non tamen se implicat illis, sed moderate et interdum se applicat talibus, cupiens expediri et Deo uniri. Ut ei, videlicet Deo, placeat cui se probavit, id est, probabilem exhibuit seu devovit, dicens cum Psalmista: Mihi adhærere Deo bonum est; et, Unam petii a Domino, hanc requiram.
paras.en: [[2:4|No man, being a soldier to God|Nemo militans Deo]], that is, for the honour and glory of God, resisting the adversaries of the truth, wrestling against his own vices and immersing himself in divine exercises, [[2:4|entangleth|implicat]], that is, involves, [[2:4|himself with secular businesses|se negotiis sæcularibus]], that is, with worldly lawsuits, affairs and riches. For by this his mind would be drawn away from that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]]. That is why care for the morrow is forbidden by Christ. For although the servant and soldier of Christ must at times handle secular business, still he does not entangle himself in it, but applies himself to such things with moderation and only now and then, longing to be freed and united to God. [[2:4|That he may please him|Ut ei, videlicet Deo, placeat]], namely God, [[2:4|to whom he hath engaged himself|cui se probavit]], that is, to whom he has shown himself approved, or has vowed himself [the Latin *se probavit* means literally "has proved himself"], saying with the Psalmist: [[Ps 72:28|it is good for me to adhere to my God|Mihi adhærere Deo bonum est]]; and, [[Ps 26:4|One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after|Unam petii a Domino, hanc requiram]].

paras.t: Idcirco autem labora ut miles Christi: Nam et qui certat in agone, id est, cum alio contendit in hujuscemodi bellico exercitio: quod et agonizantes quandoque nudi exercuerunt; non coronabitur quasi victor, nisi legitime, id est efficaciter et sicut lex agonis requirit, certaverit, omnia impedimenta pugnandi abjiciendo, quemadmodum dictum est alibi: Omnis qui in agone contendit, ab omnibus se abstinet.
paras.en: And labour as a soldier of Christ for this reason: [[2:5|For he also that striveth for the mastery|Nam et qui certat in agone]], that is, contends with another in a warlike exercise of this kind (which those who contended in the games sometimes practised naked), [[2:5|is not crowned|non coronabitur]] as victor, [[2:5|except he strive lawfully|nisi legitime certaverit]] [Denis glosses *legitime* before *certaverit*: "lawfully, that is, effectively and as the law of the contest requires"], casting off every hindrance to fighting, as is said elsewhere: [[1 Cor 9:25|every one that striveth for the mastery refraineth himself from all things|Omnis qui in agone contendit, ab omnibus se abstinet]].

paras.t: Laborantem agricolam oportet primum de fructibus percipere: id est, quemadmodum agricola diligens primo fruges suæ terræ degustat, et de eis necessaria sumit et edit; sic prædicator et pastor qui corda audientium vomere prædicationis aperit, vertit et excolit, semenque verbi cœlestis infundit, debet de sumptibus aliorum et gregis proprii sustentari. Dignus est enim operarius mercede sua. Hoc dicit Apostolus, quia superius dixit quod militans Deo non implicat se sæcularibus negotiis. Ut ergo ostendat unde prædicator et prælatus vivere debeat, adjecit similitudinem de agricola.
paras.en: [[2:6|The husbandman that laboureth must first partake of the fruits.|Laborantem agricolam oportet primum de fructibus percipere]]: that is, as a diligent husbandman first tastes the fruits of his own land, and takes from them and eats what he needs, so the preacher and pastor, who opens, turns and tills the hearts of his hearers with the ploughshare of preaching and sows in them the seed of the heavenly word, ought to be supported at the expense of others and of his own flock. [[Luke 10:7|for the labourer is worthy of his hire|Dignus est enim operarius mercede sua]]. The Apostle says this because he said above that the soldier of God does not entangle himself with secular business. So, to show what the preacher and prelate should live on, he added the comparison of the husbandman.

paras.t: Intellige, id est, discrete perpende, quæ dico, ne tibi videatur contrarietas in verbis et actibus meis: eo quod ego non accipiam sumptum ab aliis, cujus oppositum te doceo. Ego enim non accipio interdum propter rationabiles causas, ut amputem occasionem perversis. Te vero accipere volo propter rationabiles causas, quum sis infirmus, et ut Deo liberius vaces. Dabit enim tibi Dominus in omnibus quæ scribo aut facio, intellectum, id est veram ac circumspectam notitiam.
paras.en: [[2:7|Understand|Intellige]], that is, weigh with discernment, [[2:7|what I say|quæ dico]], lest there seem to thee to be a contradiction between my words and my deeds, in that I do not take support from others, while I teach thee the opposite. For I at times do not take it, for good reasons, that I may cut off the occasion from the perverse[[2 Cor 11:9||]][[2 Cor 11:12||]][[2 Cor 12:13||]][[2 Cor 12:14||]][[1 Thess 2:9||]][[2 Thess 3:8||]]. But I wish thee to take it, for good reasons: since thou art infirm, and that thou mayest be more free for God. [[2:7|for the Lord will give thee in all things|Dabit enim tibi Dominus in omnibus]] which I write or do, [[2:7|understanding|intellectum]], that is, true and circumspect knowledge.

paras.t: Denique, quatenus legitime certes consideratione futuræ coronationis, memor esto per actualem considerationem, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum resurrexisse a mortuis, natum ex semine David, secundum evangelium meum, id est secundum evangelicam annuntiationem a me administratam; in quo, id est in cujus evangelii prædicatione, laboro usque ad vincula inclusive, quibus jam vinctus in carcere jaceo, quasi male operans, id est tanquam falsa prædicans et homines fallens. Sed verbum Dei non est alligatum, id est, prædicatio mea seu doctrina non est impedita: nam verbo præsentes in carcere doceo; scriptis vero et item per discipulos meos absentes informo.
paras.en: Lastly, so that thou mayest strive lawfully by thinking on the crowning to come, [[2:8|Be mindful|memor esto]], by actually thinking on it, [[2:8|that the Lord Jesus Christ is risen again from the dead|Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum resurrexisse a mortuis]], born [[2:8|of the seed of David, according to my gospel|ex semine David, secundum evangelium meum]][[Rom 2:16||]], that is, according to the gospel message ministered by me; [[2:9|Wherein|in quo]], that is, in the preaching of which gospel, [[2:9|I labour even unto bands|laboro usque ad vincula]] inclusively [that is, as far as the chains themselves], with which I now lie bound in prison, [[2:9|as an evildoer|quasi male operans]], that is, as though preaching falsehoods and deceiving men. [[2:9|But the word of God is not bound|Sed verbum Dei non est alligatum]], that is, my preaching or teaching is not hindered: for by word I teach those present with me in prison, and by letters, and likewise through my disciples, I instruct those absent.

paras.t: Ideo omnia adversa sustineo patienter propter electos, ut et ipsi salutem consequantur, non a me, sed per ministerium meum, videlicet ut cooperer eorum saluti, quæ est in Christo Jesu sicut in objecto, datore et causa meritoria: in ejus enim visione consistit, ab ipso donatur, ipse quoque nobis promeruit eam; cum gloria cœlesti, id est, salutem consequantur cum omni beatitudine præmii accidentalis adjuncta præmio essentiali, quæ per salutem exprimitur. Vel, per salutem intelligitur felicitas viæ, per gloriam cœlestem, felicitas patriæ.
paras.en: [[2:10|Therefore I endure all things|Ideo omnia adversa sustineo]] adverse, patiently, [[2:10|for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation|propter electos, ut et ipsi salutem consequantur]], not from me but through my ministry, namely so that I may cooperate in their salvation, [[2:10|which is in Christ Jesus|quæ est in Christo Jesu]] as in its object, its giver and its meritorious cause: for it consists in the vision of Him, it is given by Him, and He also merited it for us; [[2:10|with heavenly glory|cum gloria cœlesti]], that is, that they may obtain salvation with all the bliss of the accidental reward joined to the essential reward, which is expressed by *salvation* [in scholastic terms the essential reward of heaven is the vision of God; the accidental reward is the further joys added to it]. Or, by *salvation* is understood the happiness of the way, by *heavenly glory* the happiness of the fatherland [that is, of this life's pilgrimage and of heaven].

paras.t: Fidelis sermo quem dixi et dicam. Nam si commortui sumus, id est, Christi passionibus conformamur, mundo et vitiis moriendo, ejusque vestigia digne sequendo, et convivemus cum Christo vita gratiæ in præsenti, et vita gloriæ in futuro. Si sustinemus adversa pro Christo, et conregnabimus cum eo in regno cœlorum. Si negaverimus cum verbis vel impiis factis, et ille negabit nos pertinere ad ipsum: sicut in Evangelio ait quibusdam: Nescio vos unde sitis; discedite a me, operarii iniquitatis. Propter quod rursus loquuntur: Qui negaverit me coram hominibus, denegabitur coram angelis Dei. Si non credimus ea quæ fidei sunt, ille, scilicet Deus seu Christus, fidelis, id est verus, […]test, quum ipse sit veritas. Et hoc non posse, non ad impotentiam pertinet, sed ad veram ac summam potentiam: sicut posse peccare, non ad veram potentiam, sed ad impotentiam spectat. Qui enim potest quod sibi non expedit, quanto id magis potest, tanto impotentior est et infelicior. Quemadmodum Dionysius recitat, hunc locum Elymas magus objecit Apostolo, quasi derogaret omnipotentiæ Dei, quod se ipsum negare non potest.
paras.en: [[2:11|A faithful saying|Fidelis sermo]] which I have spoken and will speak. [[2:11|for if we be dead with him|Nam si commortui sumus]], that is, are conformed to the sufferings of Christ[[2 Cor 1:7||]], dying to the world and to vices and worthily following in His footsteps, [[2:11|we shall live also with him|et convivemus]] with Christ, by the life of grace in the present and the life of glory in the future. [[2:12|If we suffer|Si sustinemus]] adversities for Christ, [[2:12|we shall also reign with him|et conregnabimus]] with Him in the kingdom of heaven. [[2:12|If we deny him|Si negaverimus]] with words or with wicked deeds, [[2:12|he will also deny us|et ille negabit nos]] to belong to Him: as in the Gospel He says to some: [[Luke 13:27|I know you not, whence you are. Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity|Nescio vos unde sitis; discedite a me, operarii iniquitatis]]. For which reason they say again: [[Luke 12:9|he that shall deny me before men shall be denied before the angels of God|Qui negaverit me coram hominibus, denegabitur coram angelis Dei]] [the margin gives Matt. x, 33; Denis's wording is that of Luke 12:9]. [[2:13|If we believe not|Si non credimus]] the things that are of faith, [[2:13|he|ille]], namely God or Christ, [[2:13|continueth faithful|fidelis]], that is, true, […] [several words are lost here; only the end of a word, *…test*, survives, presumably from the lemma *negare seipsum non potest*, "he cannot deny himself"], since He Himself is the truth. And this *not being able* belongs not to impotence but to true and supreme power: just as *being able to sin* belongs not to true power but to impotence. For he who is able to do what is not good for him is the more impotent and the more unhappy, the more he is able to do it. As Dionysius relates, Elymas the magician objected this passage to the Apostle, as though it detracted from the omnipotence of God that He cannot deny Himself.

paras.t: Hæc commone, id est, ad horum fidem et observantiam alios exhortare, testificans coram Deo, id est Deum testem invocans, vel per eum auditores tuos adjurans et obsecrans. Noli verbis contendere, cum aliis disputando seu conferendo; ad nihil enim utile est directe et ex sua natura talis verbosa contentio, nisi ad subversionem audientium, qui scandalizantur per hoc. Ideo dicit Glossa, quod non sit securum cum hæreticis disputare in publico. Non sic autem intelligendum est verbum Apostoli, quasi ad subversionem audientium utile esse, sit vera utilitas; sed tantum vult dicere, quod contentio ad nihil valet nisi ad subversionem. Ideo prorsus inutilis est et nociva ac fugienda. Unde Corinthiis dictum est: Si quis videtur contentiosus esse, nos talem consuetudinem non habemus, nec Ecclesia Dei. Ideo dicit Ambrosius: Collatio, non altercatio, esse debet inter famulos Dei.
paras.en: [[2:14|Of these things put them in mind|Hæc commone]], that is, exhort others to believe and observe these things, [[2:14|charging them before the Lord|testificans coram Deo]], that is, calling God to witness, or adjuring and beseeching thy hearers by Him. [[2:14|Contend not in words|Noli verbis contendere]], disputing or debating with others; [[2:14|for it is to no profit|ad nihil enim utile est]], directly and of its own nature, such wordy contention, [[2:14|but to the subverting of the hearers|nisi ad subversionem audientium]], who are scandalized by it. Therefore the Gloss says that it is not safe to dispute with heretics in public. But the Apostle's word is not to be understood as though being *profitable* to the subverting of the hearers were a true profit; he only means to say that contention is good for nothing except subversion. It is therefore altogether unprofitable and harmful, and to be shunned. Hence it was said to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 11:16|if any man seem to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor the Church of God|Si quis videtur contentiosus esse, nos talem consuetudinem non habemus, nec Ecclesia Dei]]. Therefore Ambrose says: Among the servants of God there should be conference, not altercation.

paras.t: Sollicite cura te ipsum probabilem, id est laudabilem et acceptum, exhibere Deo, opus Dei reverenter agendo, et in puritate conscientiæ coram Altissimo conversando, operarium inconfusibilem, id est exsecutorem virtutum irreprehensibilem, ut non metuas venire ad lucem quatenus manifestentur opera tua: recte tractantem, id est discrete proponentem, verbum veritatis, unumquemque docendo prout capere potest vel indiget.
paras.en: [[2:15|Carefully study to present thyself approved|Sollicite cura te ipsum probabilem]], that is, praiseworthy and accepted, [[2:15|unto God|exhibere Deo]], doing the work of God reverently and living before the Most High in purity of conscience, [[2:15|a workman that needeth not to be ashamed|operarium inconfusibilem]], that is, a blameless performer of the virtues, so that thou mayest not fear to come to the light, that thy works may be made manifest[[John 3:21||]] [the margin note here could not be read; the words are those of John 3:21]: [[2:15|rightly handling|recte tractantem]], that is, setting forth with discernment, [[2:15|the word of truth|verbum veritatis]], teaching each one as he can take it in, or as he needs.

paras.t: Profana autem, id est verba sanctæ Religioni contraria, et vaniloquia, devita audire vel loqui: juxta illud, Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam, et ori tuo facito ostia et seras: […] id est valde cooperantur, ad impietatem: quoniam cultum Dei impediunt, et errores graves inducunt hujusmodi verba. Sumit autem verbum, Proficiunt, impropre.
paras.en: [[2:16|profane|Profana autem]], that is, words contrary to holy Religion, [[2:16|and vain babblings|et vaniloquia]], [[2:16|shun|devita]] hearing or speaking them; according to that saying: [[Ecclus 28:28|Hedge in thy ears with thorns|Sepi aures tuas spinis]], [[Ecclus 28:28|hear not a wicked tongue|et noli audire linguam nequam]], [[Ecclus 28:28|and make doors and bars to thy mouth|et ori tuo facito ostia et seras]] [the margin's chapter and verse could not be read]: […] [some words are lost here, presumably the lemma *multum enim proficiunt*, "for they grow much"], that is, they greatly contribute, [[2:16|towards ungodliness|ad impietatem]]: since words of this kind hinder the worship of God and bring in grave errors. Now he uses the word *proficiunt* [literally "they make progress"] improperly.

paras.t: Et sermo eorum, videlicet profanorum, hæreticorum et vana loquentium, ut cancer serpit, id est, ad similitudinem morbi illius paulatim crescit, et tendit a parvo errore ad magnum. Ex quibus, id est de quorum hæreticorum infelici collegio, est Hymenæus et Philetus, qui a veritate fidei in qua olim steterunt, exciderunt, cadendo in hæresim, dicentes resurrectionem jam factam, id est, ea quæ Scriptura testatur de generali resurrectione corporum, asserentes intelligenda esse de spirituali resurrectione animarum a vitiis, quæ in Baptismo jam facta est, quotidieque impletur. Contra quos sanctus Job apertissime profitetur: Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum, et rursum circumdabor pelle mea, etc. Et subverterunt, sua fallaci expositione, quorumdam simplicium fidem.
paras.en: [[2:17|And their speech|Et sermo eorum]], namely of the profane, of heretics and of those who speak vain things, [[2:17|spreadeth like a canker|ut cancer serpit]], that is, like that disease it grows little by little, and goes on from a small error to a great one. [[2:17|of whom|Ex quibus]], that is, of which unhappy company of heretics, [[2:17|are Hymeneus|est Hymenæus]] and [[2:17|Philetus|et Philetus]], [[2:18|Who have erred from the truth|qui a veritate exciderunt]] of the faith in which they once stood [Denis's *exciderunt* is literally "have fallen away"], falling into heresy, [[2:18|saying that the resurrection is past already|dicentes resurrectionem jam factam]], that is, asserting that what Scripture testifies of the general resurrection of bodies is to be understood of the spiritual resurrection of souls from vices, which has already taken place in Baptism and is fulfilled daily. Against them holy Job most openly professes: [[Job 19:25|my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]] [Denis begins "I believe that", where the Douay-Rheims has "For I know that"], [[Job 19:26|And I shall be clothed again with my skin|et rursum circumdabor pelle mea]], etc. [[2:18|and have subverted the faith of some|et subverterunt quorumdam fidem]] [Denis's wording: "and have subverted by their deceitful exposition the faith of some simple people"].

paras.t: Sed firmum, id est, quamvis illi sic perierunt, non tamen de subversione omnium est timendum; sed firmum fundamentum Dei, id est Ecclesia in Deo fundata: quæ in præcedenti epistola dicta est firmamentum atque columna veritatis; stat firmiter in fide; habens signaculum hoc, id est, hoc quod subditur habens pro sigillo et signo certissimo quod ipsa non peribit: Cognovit Dominus qui sunt ejus, id est, Deus prædestinatos suos æternaliter cognoscit, scriptos in libro vitæ, eosque conservat et approbat. Habens quoque signaculum hoc secundum, quod sequitur: et discedat ab iniquitate, id est, peccata devitet, omnis qui nominat cum mente fideli ac munda nomen Domini. De qua nominatione dicit Apostolus: Nemo potest dicere Dominum Jesum, nisi in Spiritu Sancto. Hæc autem discessio, signum est prædestinationis et salvationis Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: [[2:19|But the sure|Sed firmum]]: that is, although those men have perished in this way, still the subversion of all is not to be feared; but [[2:19|the sure foundation of God|firmum fundamentum Dei]], that is, the Church founded in God, which in the preceding epistle is called the [[1 Tim 3:15|pillar and ground of the truth|firmamentum atque columna veritatis]], [[2:19|standeth firm|stat]] in the faith; [[2:19|having this seal|habens signaculum hoc]], that is, having what follows as a seal and most certain sign that she will not perish: [[2:19|the Lord knoweth who are his|Cognovit Dominus qui sunt ejus]], that is, God knows from eternity His predestined[[Rom 8:29||]], who are written in the book of life, and preserves and approves them. Having also this second seal, which follows: [[2:19|and let every one depart from iniquity|et discedat ab iniquitate]], that is, let him avoid sins, [[2:19|who nameth|omnis qui nominat]] with a faithful and clean mind [[2:19|the name of the Lord|nomen Domini]]. Of this naming the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 12:3|no man can say The Lord Jesus, but by the Holy Ghost|Nemo potest dicere Dominum Jesum, nisi in Spiritu Sancto]]. Now this departing is a sign of the predestination and salvation of the Church.

paras.t: Et quasi aliquis quæreret, cur Deus permittat sic quosdam perire, respondet Apostolus, ponens exemplum de grandi palatio: In magna autem domo, non solum sunt vasa aurea et argentea, pretiosa et pro usibus nobilibus facta, quæ in mensam patrisfamilias apportantur, sed et lignea et fictilia, id est etiam vilia vasa, sunt in domo hujusmodi. Et quædam quidem, id est aurea et argentea vasa, facta sunt in honorem, id est ad usus præclaros; quædam autem, id est vasa lignea et fictilia, facta sunt in contumeliam, id est ad usus immundos. Per hoc insinuatur, quod in Ecclesia (quæ est magna domus Dei), non solum sunt electi et boni, qui per vasa aurea et argentea designantur, sed etiam reprobi, qui per vilia vasa notantur. Electi autem facti sunt in honorem, id est ad gloriam sempiternam: in quibus impletur id Psalmistæ, Gloriam et magnum decorem impones super eum. Reprobi vero sunt in contumeliam, id est ad æternam confusionem ac pœnam. Et hoc totum cedit ad gloriam Creatoris: nam sicut in illis resplendet misericordia, sic in istis manifestatur divina justitia. Unumquodque oppositorum ex consideratione sui oppositi clarius elucescit.
paras.en: And as though someone should ask why God permits some to perish in this way, the Apostle answers, setting forth the example of a great palace: [[2:20|But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver|In magna autem domo, non solum sunt vasa aurea et argentea]], precious and made for noble uses, which are brought to the table of the master of the house, [[2:20|but also of wood and of earth|sed et lignea et fictilia]], that is, there are also mean vessels in a house of this kind. [[2:20|and some indeed|Et quædam quidem]], that is, the vessels of gold and silver, are made [[2:20|unto honour|in honorem]], that is, for distinguished uses; [[2:20|but some|quædam autem]], that is, the vessels of wood and earth, are made [[2:20|unto dishonour|in contumeliam]], that is, for unclean uses. By this it is hinted that in the Church (which is the great house of God) there are not only the elect and the good, who are signified by the vessels of gold and silver, but also the reprobate, who are denoted by the mean vessels. Now the elect are made unto honour, that is, for everlasting glory: in them is fulfilled that word of the Psalmist, [[Ps 20:6|glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him|Gloriam et magnum decorem impones super eum]]. But the reprobate are unto dishonour, that is, for eternal confusion and punishment. And all this redounds to the glory of the Creator: for as mercy shines forth in the former, so divine justice is shown in the latter[[Rom 9:22||]][[Rom 9:23||]]. Each of two opposites shines out more clearly from the consideration of its opposite.

paras.t: Si quis ergo emundaverit se ab istis, id est a vitiis reproborum, qui sunt in contumeliam, erit vas in honorem sanctificatum, id est, per gratiam sanctificabitur, ita ut finaliter sempiternum consequatur honorem, audiens illud a Christo: Intra in gaudium Domini tui; et utile Domino, id est ad gloriam Dei proficuum aliis, ad omne opus bonum paratum, id est a Deo dispositum et formatum ad facienda opera virtuosa.
paras.en: [[2:21|If any man therefore shall cleanse himself from these|Si quis ergo emundaverit se ab istis]], that is, from the vices of the reprobate, who are unto dishonour, [[2:21|he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified|erit vas in honorem sanctificatum]], that is, he will be sanctified by grace, so that in the end he obtains everlasting honour, hearing that word from Christ: [[Matt 25:21|Enter thou into the joy of thy lord|Intra in gaudium Domini tui]][[Matt 25:23||]]; [[2:21|and profitable to the Lord|et utile Domino]], that is, useful to others for the glory of God, [[2:21|prepared unto every good work|ad omne opus bonum paratum]], that is, disposed and formed by God for doing virtuous works.

paras.t: Juvenilia autem desideria, id est pueriles concupiscentias, fuge, videlicet consolationes carnales ac levitates. Sectare vero per jugem operationem, justitiam, quæ est præclarissima virtus: et nec est hesperus nec lucifer ita admirabilis, quantum ad virtutes morales in appetitiva potentia existentes; fidem, spem, caritatem Dei et proximi, et pacem internam et concordiam cum aliis, cum his qui invocant Dominum de corde puro. Tales nempe has virtutes sectantur.
paras.en: [[2:22|But flee thou youthful desires|Juvenilia autem desideria fuge]] [Denis glosses *desideria* before *fuge*], that is, boyish lusts: namely carnal consolations and frivolities. [[2:22|and pursue|Sectare vero]] by constant practice [[2:22|justice|justitiam]], which is the most splendid virtue, and neither the evening star nor the morning star is so wonderful [an echo of Aristotle, *Ethics* V, 1], as far as concerns the moral virtues that exist in the appetitive power; [[2:22|faith|fidem]], hope, [[2:22|charity|caritatem]] of God and of neighbour [the Douay-Rheims does not have "hope", which the Vulgate and Denis read], [[2:22|and peace|et pacem]] within, and concord with others, [[2:22|with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart|cum his qui invocant Dominum de corde puro]]. For such men pursue these virtues.

paras.t: Stultas autem et sine disciplina quæstiones, id est vanas et ineruditas, devita: sciens quia generant lites, non ædificationem in fide et moribus.
paras.en: [[2:23|foolish and unlearned questions|Stultas autem et sine disciplina quæstiones]][[1 Tim 1:4||]][[Tit 3:9||]], that is, vain and untaught ones, [[2:23|avoid|devita]]: [[2:23|knowing that they beget strifes|sciens quia generant lites]], not edification in faith and morals.

paras.t: Servum autem Domini non oportet, imo nec licet, litigare: sicut jam dictum est, Noli verbis contendere; sed mansuetum esse ad omnes, iram frenando. Unde ait Sapiens: In mansuetudine opera tua fac, et super hominum gloriam diligeris. Docilem, ut possit facile instrui, nec sit pertinax in proprio sensu, quemadmodum Christus in Evangelio loquitur: Erunt omnes docibiles Dei. Et Jacobus: Cum mansuetudine, inquit, suscipite insitum verbum.
paras.en: [[2:24|But the servant of the Lord must not|Servum autem Domini non oportet]], nay, it is not even lawful for him, [[2:24|wrangle|litigare]]: as has already been said, [[2:14|Contend not in words|Noli verbis contendere]]; [[2:24|but be mild toward all men|sed mansuetum esse ad omnes]], by bridling anger. Hence the Wise Man says: [[Ecclus 3:19|do thy works in meekness, and thou shalt be beloved above the glory of men|In mansuetudine opera tua fac, et super hominum gloriam diligeris]]. [[2:24|apt to teach|Docilem]] [Denis reads *docilem*, "teachable", where the Vulgate has *docibilem*], so that he can be readily taught, and is not obstinate in his own opinion: as Christ says in the Gospel: [[John 6:45|And they shall all be taught of God|Erunt omnes docibiles Dei]]. And James: [[Jas 1:21|with meekness|Cum mansuetudine]], he says, [[Jas 1:21|receive the ingrafted word|suscipite insitum verbum]].

paras.t: Patientem in adversis. Cum modestia, id est cum discretione ac moderamine, sine perturbatione et impetu, corripientem eos qui resistunt veritati, id est rebelles Deo atque justitiæ: de quibus Job ait, Ipsi fuerunt rebelles lumini: […], id est ut tandem aliquando, det illis inobedientibus Deus pœnitentiam, id est gratiam pœnitendi de pristinis malis, ad cognoscendam veritatem fidei et doctrinæ. Purgati enim a vitiis per pœnitentiam, apti sunt illuminationi divinæ, eamque recipiunt, quum aliud nihil dividat mentem rationalem a Deo nisi peccatum. Propter quod Isaias ait: Hic est omnis fructus, ut deleatur iniquitas; et rursus, Iniquitates vestræ diviserunt inter Deum vestrum et vos. Jeremias quoque testatur: Peccata vestra prohibuerunt bonum a vobis. Et resipiscant a diaboli laqueis, id est peccatis atque erroribus: quibus animæ a dæmone capiuntur, prout Scriptura dicit, Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur; a quo diabolo captivi tenentur, id est dominationi et jugo dæmonis ac peccati subjecti, ad ipsius diaboli voluntatem, id est sicut diabolo placet et ad exsequendam voluntatem ipsius.
paras.en: [[2:24|patient|Patientem]] in adversities. [[2:25|With modesty|Cum modestia]], that is, with discretion and moderation, without agitation or vehemence, [[2:25|admonishing them that resist the truth|corripientem eos qui resistunt veritati]], that is, those rebellious against God and justice, of whom Job says: [[Job 24:13|They have been rebellious to the light|Ipsi fuerunt rebelles lumini]] [the margin gives Job xxxi, 13; the words are Job 24:13]: […] [the first word of this lemma is lost; the Vulgate has *nequando*, "if peradventure"], that is, that at length at some time [[2:25|God may give them|det illis]], the disobedient, [[2:25|repentance|Deus pœnitentiam]], that is, the grace of repenting of their former evils, [[2:25|to know the truth|ad cognoscendam veritatem]] of faith and doctrine. For being cleansed of vices by repentance, they are fit for divine enlightenment and receive it, since nothing else divides the rational mind from God but sin. For which reason Isaias says: [[Is 27:9|this is all the fruit, that the sin thereof should be taken away|Hic est omnis fructus, ut deleatur iniquitas]] [Denis's wording: "that iniquity be blotted out"]; and again, [[Is 59:2|your iniquities have divided between you and your God|Iniquitates vestræ diviserunt inter Deum vestrum et vos]] [the margin gives Ibid. ix, 2, a misreading of lix, 2]. Jeremias also testifies: [[Jer 5:25|your sins have withholden good things from you|Peccata vestra prohibuerunt bonum a vobis]]. [[2:26|And they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil|Et resipiscant a diaboli laqueis]], that is, from sins and errors, by which souls are caught by the demon, as Scripture says: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]]; [[2:26|by whom they are held captive|a quo diabolo captivi tenentur]], by the devil, that is, subject to the dominion and yoke of the demon and of sin, [[2:26|at his will|ad ipsius diaboli voluntatem]], the devil's, that is, as it pleases the devil, and to carry out his will.

3.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI TERTII : HOC AUTEM SCITO, QUOD IN NOVISSIMIS DIEBUS, ETC.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: Know also this, that in the last days, etc.

paras.t: PRÆTEREA docet Apostolus Timotheum debere sollicitum esse propter futura pericula. Hoc autem scito, quod in novissimis diebus, circa Antichristi adventum, instabunt tempora periculosa. Erit enim tunc tribulatio talis, qualis non fuit ab exordio mundi. Tunc namque Ecclesia persecutionem sustinebit a tribus gravissimis hostibus simul, a quibus ante successive afflicta est, utputa a tyrannis, ab hæreticis, falsisque fratribus.
paras.en: Moreover, the Apostle teaches Timothy that he ought to be watchful on account of the dangers to come. [[3:1|Know also this, that in the last days|Hoc autem scito, quod in novissimis diebus]], about the time of the coming of Antichrist, [[3:1|shall come dangerous times|instabunt tempora periculosa]]. [[Matt 24:21|For there shall be then great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the world|Erit enim tunc tribulatio talis, qualis non fuit ab exordio mundi]]. For then the Church will suffer persecution from three most grievous enemies at once, by whom she was afflicted before one after another: namely from tyrants, from heretics, and from false brethren.

paras.t: Erunt homines se ipsos amantes, amore carnali, privato et pessimo, quaerentes solum bona delectabilia et utilia, non honesta, cupidi, id est avari, elati, id est ambitiosi, superbi, quantum ad appetitum excellentiae in temporalibus, blasphemi in Deum et Sanctos, parentibus non obedientes, ingrati Deo, magistris et parentibus, quibus non potest reddi æquivalens, scelesti, id est magnis peccatis obnoxii; sine affectione, id est corde frigidi a calore amoris divini, sine pace interiori et exteriori, id est turbulenti, criminatores, alios inordinate accusando, videntes alienas festucas, non proprias trabes: incontinentes, id est luxuriosi, immites, id est iracundi, sine benignitate, id est fraterna compassione, proditores justorum: proditores, id est crudeles, juxta illud: Viscera impiorum crudelia; tumidi contra Deum, sicut Job ait: Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur: voluptatum carnalium, scilicet gulæ et luxuriæ, amatores magis quam Dei, præponentes carnalia spiritualibus ac divinis; habentes speciem quidem pietatis, id est simulatam sanctitatem et apparentiam veræ Religionis assumentes, venientes videlicet in vestimentis ovium, virtutem autem ejus abnegantes, id est vigorem seu exsistentiam pietatis abjicientes, quum sint hypocritæ, et intus lupi rapaces.
paras.en: [[3:2|Men shall be lovers of themselves|Erunt homines se ipsos amantes]], with a carnal, private and most wicked love, seeking only the goods that are pleasant and useful, not those that are honourable [that is, good in themselves, the *bonum honestum* of the schools, as against what merely pleases or profits]; [[3:2|covetous|cupidi]], that is, avaricious; [[3:2|haughty|elati]], that is, ambitious; [[3:2|proud|superbi]] as regards the desire to excel in temporal things; [[3:2|blasphemers|blasphemi]] against God and the Saints; [[3:2|disobedient to parents|parentibus non obedientes]]; [[3:2|ungrateful|ingrati]] to God, to their teachers and to their parents, to whom no equivalent return can be made; [[3:2|wicked|scelesti]], that is, guilty of great sins; [[3:3|Without affection|sine affectione]], that is, cold of heart, without the warmth of divine love; [[3:3|without peace|sine pace]], within and without, that is, turbulent; [[3:3|slanderers|criminatores]], accusing others inordinately, seeing other men's motes and not their own beams[[Matt 7:3||]]; [[3:3|incontinent|incontinentes]], that is, lustful; [[3:3|unmerciful|immites]], that is, given to anger; [[3:3|without kindness|sine benignitate]], that is, without brotherly compassion; [[3:4|Traitors|proditores]] of the just; [[3:4|stubborn|proditores]] [the print repeats *proditores* here, where the Vulgate has *protervi*, "stubborn"], that is, cruel, according to that saying: [[Prov 12:10|the bowels of the wicked are cruel|Viscera impiorum crudelia]]; [[3:4|puffed up|tumidi]] against God, as Job says: [[Job 11:12|A vain man is lifted up into pride|Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur]]; [[3:4|lovers of pleasure|voluptatum]] (carnal pleasures, namely of gluttony and lust) [[3:4|more than of God|amatores magis quam Dei]], preferring carnal things to spiritual and divine; [[3:5|Having an appearance indeed of godliness|habentes speciem quidem pietatis]], that is, putting on a feigned holiness and the appearance of true religion, coming, that is, [[Matt 7:15|in the clothing of sheep|in vestimentis ovium]]; [[3:5|but denying the power thereof|virtutem autem ejus abnegantes]], that is, casting away the vigour or the very being of godliness, since they are hypocrites, and inwardly [[Matt 7:15|ravening wolves|lupi rapaces]].

paras.t: Et hos, id est typos et prædecessores istorum qui prædictis vitiis polluuntur, devita. Ex his enim, id est de horum catalogo, sunt qui penetrant domos, id est, secretiora loca domorum ingrediuntur, ut in occulto suos errores disseminent: nam omnis qui male agit, odit lucem; et captivas ducunt mulierculas, id est, suis erroribus involvunt feminas in domibus residentes, oneratas peccatis, id est peccatrices, et ideo decipi dignas, quæ ducuntur variis desideriis, id est, diversis concupiscentiis et curiositatibus agitantur, propter rationis debilitatem et animi instabilitatem; semper discentes aliquid novi vel Scripturas, et nunquam ad scientiam, id est notitiam salutarem, veritatis pervenientes, quoniam inordinate se habent in addiscendo, et curiosa ac frivola magis quam fructuosa ac necessaria discunt.
paras.en: [[3:5|Now these|Et hos]], that is, the types and forerunners of those who are defiled with the vices just named, [[3:5|avoid|devita]]. [[3:6|For of these sort|Ex his enim]], that is, of their number, [[3:6|are they who creep into houses|sunt qui penetrant domos]], that is, enter the more secret parts of houses, to sow their errors in hiding: for [[John 3:20|every one that doth evil hateth the light|omnis qui male agit, odit lucem]]; [[3:6|and lead captive silly women|et captivas ducunt mulierculas]], that is, entangle in their errors women who stay at home, [[3:6|laden with sins|oneratas peccatis]], that is, sinful women, and therefore deserving to be deceived, [[3:6|who are led away with divers desires|quæ ducuntur variis desideriis]], that is, are driven about by divers concupiscences and curiosities, through weakness of reason and instability of mind; [[3:7|Ever learning|semper discentes]] something new, or the Scriptures, [[3:7|and never attaining to the knowledge|et nunquam ad scientiam]], that is, the knowledge that saves, [[3:7|of the truth|veritatis pervenientes]]: because they are disordered in their learning, and learn curious and frivolous things rather than fruitful and necessary ones.

paras.t: Quemadmodum autem Jannes et Mambres, qui erant duo fratres et magi Pharaonis: quorum nomina, secundum Glossam, sumpsit Apostolus ex libris apocryphis. Sed hoc certum arbitror, quod auctoritati apocryphorum non innitebatur Apostolus, sicut nec Judas apostolus in sua Canonica, allegans verba Enoch, quæ in apocryphis scripta sunt. Sed uterque eorum aliunde, vel ex revelatione divina certificatus erat de veritate verborum quæ introduxerunt. Quemadmodum ergo hi restiterunt Moysi, facientes signa coram Pharaone sicut et Moyses, usque ad tertium signum, in quo omnis pulvis terræ Ægypti versus est in sciniphes: ubi deficientes hi magi, dixerunt, Digitus Dei est hic; ita et hi seductores, domorum penetralia introeuntes, resistunt veritati fidei christianæ, homines corrupti mente, id est intellectu depravati, reprobi circa fidem, id est a fide errantes. Sed ultra non proficient, id est, non diu alios fallent; insipientia enim, id est perfidia eorum, manifesta erit omnibus Catholicis, sicut et illorum magorum fallacia manifestata est, quando a Moyse victi sunt, et plagas Dei senserunt. Loquitur autem Apostolus præcipue contra hæreticos Asiæ, quos prævidit a beatissimo evangelista Joanne confutandos. Et tamen de aliis hæreticis accipi potest, qui frequenter a Catholicis superati et eradicati leguntur, magis divina virtute quam potestate humana.
paras.en: [[3:8|Now as Jannes and Mambres|Quemadmodum autem Jannes et Mambres]], who were two brothers and magicians of Pharao; whose names, according to the Gloss, the Apostle took from apocryphal books. But this I hold for certain, that the Apostle did not rest on the authority of the apocrypha, as neither did Jude the apostle in his Canonical Epistle when he alleged the words of Enoch, which are written in the apocrypha[[Jude 1:14||]]. Rather, each of them had been assured from elsewhere, or by divine revelation, of the truth of the words they brought in. As then these [[3:8|resisted Moses|restiterunt Moysi]], doing signs before Pharao as Moses also did[[Ex 7:11||]], up to the third sign, in which all the dust of the land of Egypt was turned into sciniphs[[Ex 8:16||]] [gnats], where these magicians failed and said, [[Ex 8:19|This is the finger of God|Digitus Dei est hic]]; [[3:8|so these also|ita et hi]] seducers, who make their way into the inner rooms of houses, [[3:8|resist the truth|resistunt veritati]] of the Christian faith, [[3:8|men corrupted in mind|homines corrupti mente]], that is, depraved in understanding, [[3:8|reprobate concerning the faith|reprobi circa fidem]], that is, straying from the faith [the margin gives Exod. vii, 11 and following; viii, 1–19]. [[3:9|But they shall proceed no farther|Sed ultra non proficient]], that is, they will not deceive others for long; [[3:9|for their folly|insipientia enim]], that is, their faithlessness, [[3:9|shall be manifest to all men|manifesta erit omnibus]], to all Catholics, even as the deceit of those magicians also was made manifest, when they were overcome by Moses and felt the plagues of God. Now the Apostle speaks chiefly against the heretics of Asia, who he foresaw would be confuted by the most blessed evangelist John. And yet it can be understood of other heretics, who, as we read, have often been overcome and rooted out by Catholics, more by divine power than by human might.

paras.t: Tu autem, o Timothee, assecutus es, id est, discendo adeptus vel operando imitatus es, meam doctrinam, id est scientiam Scripturarum sanctarum, institutionem, quantum ad mores laudabiles, propositum, id est intentionem, fidem, longanimitatem in exspectatione cœlestium promissorum, dilectionem, patientiam, persecutiones foris illatas, passiones ab intra exortas; qualia tormenta mihi facta, id est inflicta, sunt Antiochiæ, Iconii, Lystris. Per has tres urbes, alia loca in quibus persecutionem pertulit, intelliguntur. Quales persecutiones, videlicet multas et magnas, sustinui. Et ex omnibus eripuit me Dominus, præservando a morte corporis, et ab impatientia animæ, ita ut dicere valeam cum Psalmista: Quantas ostendisti mihi tribulationes multas et malas! et conversus vivificasti me, et de abyssis terræ iterum reduxisti me.
paras.en: [[3:10|But thou|Tu autem]], O Timothy, [[3:10|hast fully known|assecutus es]], that is, hast attained by learning or imitated by doing [the Latin *assequi* means both to follow closely and to attain], [[3:10|my doctrine|meam doctrinam]], that is, the knowledge of the holy Scriptures; [[3:10|manner of life|institutionem]], as regards praiseworthy conduct; [[3:10|purpose|propositum]], that is, intention; [[3:10|faith|fidem]] [[3:10|longsuffering|longanimitatem]] in awaiting the heavenly promises, [[3:10|love|dilectionem]], [[3:10|patience|patientiam]], [[3:11|Persecutions|persecutiones]] inflicted from without, [[3:11|afflictions|passiones]] arising from within: [[3:11|such|qualia]] torments [[3:11|as came upon me|mihi facta]], that is, were inflicted on me, [[3:11|at Antioch, at Iconium and at Lystra|Antiochiæ, Iconii, Lystris]]. By these three cities are understood the other places in which he suffered persecution[[Acts 13:50||]][[Acts 14:5||]][[Acts 14:18||]] [the margin gives Acts xiii, 14, 45, 50; xiv, 1–5, 6–18]. [[3:11|what persecutions|Quales persecutiones]], that is, many and great, [[3:11|I endured|sustinui]]. [[3:11|and out of them all the Lord delivered me|Et ex omnibus eripuit me Dominus]], preserving me from death of body and from impatience of soul, so that I can say with the Psalmist: [[Ps 70:20|How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth|Quantas ostendisti mihi tribulationes multas et malas! et conversus vivificasti me, et de abyssis terræ iterum reduxisti me]].

paras.t: Et omnes qui volunt voluntate efficaci, pie, id est religiose et sancte, vivere in Christo, id est secundum doctrinam et voluntatem Christi, persecutionem patientur a mundo, carne vel dæmone. Per multas enim tribulationes oportet nos intrare regnum cœlorum. Unde Judith ait: Omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles. Mali autem homines et seductores, qui sedent in cathedra pestilentiæ, proficient, id est tendent, in pejus, quemadmodum scriptum est: Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum. De minoribus quippe peccatis procedunt ad graviora, quoniam unum peccatum disponit ad aliud, estque peccatum et pœna peccati. Errantes a via veritatis atque justitiæ, et in errorem mittentes alios quos pervertunt.
paras.en: [[3:12|And all that will|Et omnes qui volunt]], with an effectual will, [[3:12|live godly|pie]], that is, religiously and holily, [[3:12|in Christ|vivere in Christo]], that is, according to the teaching and will of Christ, [[3:12|shall suffer persecution|persecutionem patientur]] from the world, the flesh or the devil. For [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom|Per multas enim tribulationes oportet nos intrare regnum]] of heaven [Denis has *regnum cœlorum*, the kingdom of heaven; the Vulgate, *regnum Dei*]. Hence Judith says: [[Jdt 8:23|all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful|Omnes qui placuerunt Deo, per multas tribulationes transierunt fideles]]. [[3:13|But evil men and seducers|Mali autem homines et seductores]], who sit in the chair of pestilence[[Ps 1:1||]], [[3:13|shall grow|proficient]], that is, shall tend, [[3:13|worse and worse|in pejus]], as it is written: [[Ecclus 3:29|the sinner will add sin to sin|Peccator adjiciet ad peccandum]]. For they go on from lesser sins to graver ones, since one sin disposes to another, and is both a sin and the punishment of sin. They go [[3:13|erring|Errantes]] from the way of truth and justice, [[3:13|and driving into error|et in errorem mittentes]] others, whom they pervert.

paras.t: Tu vero permane usque in finem fide et opere, in his quæ didicisti, id est in documentis quæ tibi proposui, et credita, id est commissa, sunt tibi, exigenda a te cum spirituali usura; sciens, id est diligenter advertens, a quo didiceris, puta a me Christi apostolo, cujus doctrina tibi ambigua esse non debet. Permanere quoque debes in his, et quia ab infantia, id est adolescentia, sacras litteras, id est scripturas legis et Prophetarum, nosti per studium, quæ te possunt instruere formaliter in his quæ pertinent ad salutem, per fidem, id est mediante et cooperante fide, quæ est in Christo Jesu, id est, quæ de Christo habetur, sine qua fide nemo ad salutem perducitur.
paras.en: [[3:14|But continue thou|Tu vero permane]] to the end, in faith and in work, [[3:14|in those things which thou hast learned|in his quæ didicisti]], that is, in the teachings I have set before thee, [[3:14|and which have been committed|et credita]], that is, entrusted, [[3:14|to thee|sunt tibi]], to be required of thee with spiritual usury[[Luke 19:23||]]; [[3:14|Knowing|sciens]] that is, carefully considering, [[3:14|of whom thou hast learned|a quo didiceris]], namely from me, the apostle of Christ, whose doctrine ought not to be doubtful to thee. Thou oughtest also to continue in them [[3:15|because from thy infancy|quia ab infantia]], that is, from youth, [[3:15|thou hast known|nosti]] by study [[3:15|the holy scriptures|sacras litteras]], that is, the writings of the Law and of the Prophets, [[3:15|which can instruct thee|quæ te possunt instruere]] formally in the things that pertain [[3:15|to salvation by the faith|ad salutem, per fidem]], that is, with faith as the means and working with them, [[3:15|which is in Christ Jesus|quæ est in Christo Jesu]], that is, which is held concerning Christ, without which faith no one is brought to salvation[[Heb 11:6||]].

paras.t: Porro, quod sacræ litteræ erudire te valeant, patet: nam, Omnis scriptura divinitus inspirata, id est tota Scriptura canonica a Spiritu Sancto infusa, non humanitus adinventa, utilis est ad docendum ignaros, ad arguendum, id est ad probandum ea quæ fidem concernunt, ad corripiendum injustos seu negligentes, ad erudiendum proficientes in justitia, id est ad obtinendam perfectionem justitiæ; ut perfectus sit, secundum modum viatorum, et prout ad salutem requiritur, vel in operibus supererogationis, servando consilia scripturæ novi Testamenti, homo Dei, hoc est cultor devotus, ad omne opus bonum prosequendum instructus per Scripturas.
paras.en: Further, that the sacred letters are able to instruct thee is plain: for [[3:16|All scripture, inspired of God|Omnis scriptura divinitus inspirata]], that is, the whole canonical Scripture, infused by the Holy Ghost and not devised by man, [[3:16|is profitable to teach|utilis est ad docendum]] the ignorant, [[3:16|to reprove|ad arguendum]], that is, to prove the things that concern the faith, [[3:16|to correct|ad corripiendum]] the unjust or negligent, [[3:16|to instruct|ad erudiendum]] those who are making progress [[3:16|in justice|in justitia]], that is, for obtaining the perfection of justice; that he [[3:17|may be perfect|ut perfectus sit]], after the manner of wayfarers [*viatores*: those still on the way to heaven, as against the blessed who have reached it], and as is required for salvation, or else in works of supererogation, by keeping the counsels of the scripture of the New Testament: [[3:17|the man of God|homo Dei]], that is, his devout worshipper, [[3:17|furnished|instructus]] by the Scriptures [[3:17|to every good work|ad omne opus bonum]] to be carried out.
